classification.difficultyReason: Read the neighbour relationships from the chain, express the outside unknowns through the middle one and substitute into its equation.

content.prompt: Find the values of $x$, $y$ and $z$ in the figure below if each of the unknowns is equal to the sum of its neighbours.

spec.description: Five unshaded circles in a horizontal chain, joined by short straight connectors at adjacent boundaries. Decorative cyan outlines and grey connectors are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: Labels from left to right are 1, x, y, z, 10. Adjacency gives x=1+y, y=x+z and z=y+10.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied endpoint values and unknown labels appear.

answer.short:
$(x,y,z)=(-10,-11,-1)$.

Express $x$ and $z$ in terms of $y$, then substitute into $y=x+z$.
answer.worked:
From the neighbouring circles,
$$\begin{align*}
x&=1+y\\
y&=x+z\\
z&=y+10.
\end{align*}$$
Substitute the expressions for $x$ and $z$ into the middle equation:
$$\begin{align*}
y&=(1+y)+(y+10)\\
y&=2y+11\\
-y&=11\\
y&=-11.
\end{align*}$$
Then
$$\begin{align*}
x&=1+(-11)\\
x&=-10\\
z&=-11+10\\
z&=-1.
\end{align*}$$
Thus $(x,y,z)=(-10,-11,-1)$.
